title: Kidney Tissue from RUUO Mice Replicate_1
characteristics_ch1: collection time after end of stress (obstruction): 0d
treatment_protocol_ch1: Mice were anesthetized and subjected to unilateral obstruction. The left ureter was clipped with a microvascular clamp to generate an obstructed kidney for either 1 day or 5 days. Kidney was collected at 0, 10 days and 28 days after clamp was removed. For each time point additional mice underwent dissection of the left ureter without ligation to serve as sham controls.
extract_protocol_ch1: Total RNA extracted using Trizol following manufacturer's instructions
label_protocol_ch1: 5 µg of total RNA were primed with T7 Promoter Primer at 65°C for 10 min, then reversed transcribed at 40°C for 2 h in the presence of MMLV-RT, and 10 mM dNTP, Cy3- or Cy5-label
treatment_protocol_ch2: Mice were anesthetized and subjected to unilateral obstruction. For each time point additional mice underwent dissection of the left ureter without ligation to serve as sham controls.
extract_protocol_ch2: Total RNA extracted using Trizol following manufacturer's instructions
label_protocol_ch2: 5 µg of total RNA were primed with T7 Promoter Primer at 65°C for 10 min, then reversed transcribed at 40°C for 2 h in the presence of MMLV-RT, and 10 mM dNTP, Cy3- or Cy5-label
hyb_protocol: Oligoarray control targets and hybridization buffer (Agilent In Situ Hybridization Kit Plus) were added, and samples were applied to microarrays enclosed in Agilent Hybridization Chamber Kit. After hybridization, slides were washed sequential
scan_protocol: Scanned on an Agilent p/n G2565BA scanner.
Images were quantified using Agilent Feature Extraction Software (version A.8.5.1.1).
description: Biological replicate 1 of 36. Kidney tissue, harvested at 0min after 1 day  RUUO.
data_processing: Agilent Feature Extraction Software (A. 7.0.1) was used for background subtraction and LOWESS normalization.
